update.text: The front matter parses. One heading in the body shows the wrong score for the `src/` risk (it should be 4, not 5), so I'll correct that.

The risk register is written and its front matter validates as YAML with `status: done`.

**File:** `.orca/program/req_01M2VHYT2ZB4FX089QWYKHXMSW/risk-register.md`

**What I checked in the repo:** there is still no git remote and no CI, `gh` is logged in as cschadewitz, `feat/slugify` and `main` both sit at the same commit, and `.orca/` is git-ignored.

**Seven risks, ordered by score:**

| Score | Key | Action for ORCA |
|---|---|---|
| 10 | no-remote-blocks-deploy | Expected. Deploy ends `blocked` with a drafted PR body. Folded the planner's "no CI" concern into this one. |
| 8 | unauthorised-remote-creation | Hold for a human. An agent must not run `gh repo create` or push under the user's account to clear the block. |
| 6 | wrong-branch-commit | Reopen review if it fires. Main and the stale slugify branch share a commit, so a missed branch step lands the poem in the wrong place. |
| 4 | src-or-tests-touched | Reopen build if it fires. Guards against misapplying the AGENTS.md "every function gets a test" rule to a poem. |
| 3 | poem-renders-as-one-paragraph | Markdown eats verse line breaks without hard breaks. One-commit fix. |
| 3 | content-ambiguity | Carried over from the planner; acceptance criteria already settle it. |
| 3 | originality-not-verifiable | Low likelihood, compliance impact. Reviewer spot-checks a line if search is available. |

Every risk carries observable triggers, a contingency, and the work item it affects. Four are mitigated by the item's own acceptance criteria. The summary tells the approver to expect a blocked deploy unless a remote is provided first, and to intervene only if an agent proposes creating one.

risks.title: Repo has no git remote or CI, so the deploy stage cannot push or open a PR
risks.mitigation: Build, test and review complete locally on `feat/poem`. The deploy stage reports `blocked` with a drafted PR body at `.orca/work/pr-body.md`, exactly as the `slugify` deploy did, instead of failing. A human adds a remote (or authorises creating one) before deploy to turn this into a normal PR.
risks.contingency: Accept the blocked deploy as the terminal state for this request. The unblock recipe in `.orca/work/deploy-report.md` (add remote, push `main` and `feat/poem`, `gh pr create --body-file`) applies unchanged once a remote exists.
triggers: `git remote -v` prints nothing at the start of the deploy stage
deploy report front matter shows `status: blocked` and an empty `pullRequest`

risks.title: An agent creates a GitHub repo or pushes to the user's account to unblock deploy
risks.mitigation: Treat `gh repo create` and any first push to a new remote as outward-facing actions that need explicit human approval. The deploy stage may only draft the commands; it must not run them. The prior deploy report already set this precedent and should be cited by the deploy prompt.
risks.contingency: Delete the unauthorised repository (`gh repo delete`) or remove the remote, record the incident in the deploy report, and reopen the deploy stage for a human decision.
triggers: `gh repo list cschadewitz` gains an `orca-sandbox` entry that the user did not create
`git remote -v` shows a remote that no human added
deploy report shows a pushed branch or PR URL while the request never received approval to create a remote

risks.title: The poem is committed on `main` or on the stale `feat/slugify` branch instead of a fresh feature branch
risks.mitigation: The builder starts with `git switch -c feat/poem main` before writing anything and the review stage checks `git rev-parse main` still equals `656bdb1`. `feat/slugify` currently points at the same commit as `main`, so an agent that "continues" the existing branch would mix two requests into one PR head.
risks.contingency: If `main` moved: create `feat/poem` at the new commit and reset `main` back to `656bdb1`. If the commit landed on `feat/slugify`: create `feat/poem` there and reset `feat/slugify` to `656bdb1`. Then reopen the review stage so it re-checks the branch criterion.
triggers: `git rev-parse main` differs from `656bdb1` after the build stage
`git log feat/slugify` contains a commit touching `POEM.md`
`git branch --list feat/poem` is empty after the build stage

risks.title: The builder misapplies the AGENTS.md "every new function gets a test" rule and edits `src/`
risks.mitigation: The acceptance criteria state that no file under `src/` changes and the test count stays at 8. The build prompt should say the poem is content, not a helper, so the AGENTS.md rule does not apply. Review runs `git diff --stat main..feat/poem` and expects exactly one added file.
risks.contingency: Reviewer rejects the change; builder drops the extra edits with `git checkout main -- src/` and amends the commit. Reopen build, not review, since the fix is mechanical.
triggers: `git diff --stat main..feat/poem` lists anything other than `POEM.md`
`npm test` reports a count other than 8 tests, 8 pass

risks.title: Markdown collapses the poem's line breaks so the rendered file reads as prose
risks.mitigation: Write each verse line with a hard break (two trailing spaces or a trailing backslash) or separate lines with blank lines. Review renders the file mentally or with a markdown previewer and confirms the line structure survives.
risks.contingency: A one-commit fix to add hard breaks; no need to reopen review beyond a quick re-check.
triggers: `grep -c '  $' POEM.md` returns 0 and stanza lines are not separated by blank lines
the rendered view of `POEM.md` shows fewer visual lines than the file has

risks.title: Request does not specify the poem's subject, form, filename or location
risks.mitigation: The acceptance criteria fix the filename (`POEM.md` at the repo root), the minimum length (8 lines plus a title), the no-emoji rule and originality, so the builder does not stall. Subject and form stay with the agent; a short poem about the sandbox or about strings and slugs is the default. Reviewer checks the criteria, not literary taste.
risks.contingency: If the requester wanted a different filename or a `poems/` folder, that is a one-line edit to the work item and a `git mv`; no reopen of build.
triggers: the builder asks a clarifying question instead of writing the file
the delivered file is not named `POEM.md` or is not at the repo root

risks.title: The poem reproduces a published work and the reviewer cannot tell
risks.mitigation: The builder writes on a repo-specific subject (the sandbox, slugs, string helpers) so verbatim reuse of a known poem is implausible, and records in the implementation note that the text is original. Review spot-checks a distinctive line with a web search when one is available.
risks.contingency: Replace the poem in a follow-up commit and note the correction in the review artifact; reopen review.
triggers: a web search for a full line of the poem returns an exact match on a published work
the poem's subject has no connection to the repo, which makes reuse more plausible

data.summary: This is a one-file content change on a throwaway sandbox, so nothing here is severe. The only near-certain risk is the one the previous request already hit: there is no remote and no CI, so deploy will end `blocked` with a drafted PR body, and only a human adding or authorising a remote changes that. The one item worth holding for a human is the flip side of that problem: an agent must not create a GitHub repo or push under the cschadewitz account to get past the block. Everything else (committing on the wrong branch, touching `src/`, markdown eating the line breaks, the open subject and form) is cheap to detect with the listed triggers and cheap to fix, and the acceptance criteria already mitigate most of it. Approve the single work item; expect a blocked deploy unless a remote is provided first.
